title: Profile spec
description: The one file a profile publishes, which makes spec.md §10 items 1 to 6 machine-readable. The mechanism reads it to run the core rules (§12) without any profile code, and a profile's own suite program reads it to run the rules beside them. Field strictness is `additionalProperties: false` here and in the profile's own payload schemas, and nowhere else (§10).

mechanism.description: The mechanism revision this profile was written against (§13).

protocolVersion.description: §6: the `<namespace>/<revision>` string the handshake must answer with, and the only version this file describes.

manifest.description: §11: the manifest's filename inside a plugin package. The mechanism reads `command`, `install`, `build`, and `conformance` from it.

methods.description: §10 item 2: the method set, with the committed schema for every request's params and every response's result. `handshake` is the mechanism's and must not be declared here.

propertyNames.description: kebab-case, and `handshake` is the mechanism's method, not the profile's.

params.description: Schema for the request's `params`. Name a file whose root schema rejects the member being absent, if the method takes no parameters: §3 omits `params` rather than sending null.

requiresCapability.description: §12 item 3: when the handshake does not declare this capability, a rule that calls this method is not applicable rather than a violation. A method gated by nothing is expected of every plugin.

deadlineField.description: §9: the params field carrying `deadlineMs` for this method, when it carries one. A rule that calls this method fills it from the manifest's `conformance.deadlineMs`.

capabilities.description: §10 item 3: the profile's capability vocabulary, and what the host does when a plugin does not declare each one. An empty object means the profile declares none, and then no rule is ever not applicable for a missing capability.

ifAbsent.description: The host's behaviour when the handshake omits this capability, in one sentence. It is the reason a rule is counted not applicable.

mapping.description: §10 item 4 and §8: the domain meaning of each loss reason the mechanism defines. Every reason must be mapped, because a host that leaves one unmapped reports a lost plugin as no finding at all.

added.description: §8: loss reasons this profile adds, named so a report can say which mechanism named them.

emitter.description: §12 item 1: the fixture emitter, run as `<argv> --out <dir>`. It produces inputs only; the suite produces results.

suite.description: §12 item 6: the profile's own suite program, run as `<argv> --out <dir>` after the mechanism wrote that directory's `profile.json` and `manifest.json`. It writes `verdicts.json`. It is a program and not a file format, exactly as the emitter is, because a profile's own rules need arbitrary logic and the mechanism is not a programming language.

deadlineMs.description: §9 and §11: the deadline one driven invocation is given. The manifest's own `conformance.deadlineMs` overrides it, and 1000 is the default when neither is set.

rules.description: §10 item 6 and §12: the profile's own rules, in the order the suite reports them. The six core rules come from `spec/core-rules.json` and must not be repeated here, because a profile that restates a core rule gets two verdicts for one check.

id.description: Stable across releases: a report a plugin author has kept is compared on this id.

expectation.description: What the plugin must do, in one sentence, in the same voice as `spec/core-rules.json`.

dependsOn.description: §12 item 3: rules whose violation makes this one impossible to run. Those are counted not applicable here, and never as passes.

defect.description: §12 item 4: either the scripted defect that makes exactly this rule report a violation, or an honest statement that no such defect exists yet and why.

argv.description: A program and its arguments, run verbatim, as §11 runs a plugin's `command`.

schemaFile.description: A committed JSON Schema file, resolved beside this file. Draft 2020-12, §10 item 2.

ruleId.description: kebab-case, so a report line and a rule id are the same string.

run.description: How to start the plugin with the defect in place. Usually the manifest's `command` under an environment variable or a wrapper the profile's reference plugin reads; `env` entries are written beside it as `NAME=value` arguments are not, so the mechanism passes them to the child.

env.description: Variables set on the defective plugin's process, as `NAME=value`.

expectViolation.description: The exact set of rules this defect must make report a violation. A defect that fires two rules proves neither.

unverified.description: §12 item 4, stated instead of a defect: why none exists yet. A rule reported here is shown as unverified in the report, which is the honest alternative to a pass that nothing has tested.
